sp-core.name: Signal processing core
sp-core.length: 10 courses, about 3.3 years at two a term
sp-core.goal: The purest path to detection and estimation mastery. Nothing but the mathematics of pulling structure out of noise.
sp-core.tradeoff: No radio frequency content at all. You will be excellent at the algorithms and unable to say why the receiver missed the signal.

sp-rf.name: Signals and RF, balanced
sp-rf.length: 10 courses, about 3.3 years at two a term
sp-rf.goal: Split across both of your specialisations, so you can argue with a signal processing engineer and an antenna engineer in the same meeting.
sp-rf.tradeoff: Half the depth of either pure track. Adaptive filtering and multirate both fall off the list.

collector-10.name: Collection systems, in ten
collector-10.length: 10 courses, about 3.3 years at two a term
collector-10.goal: The device end to end at degree length: fields, receiver, programmable logic, software radio, and the exploitation on top.
collector-10.tradeoff: Something has to give at ten courses, and what gives is the aperture. No antenna course fits. Take the long collector track if you want to design the antenna too.

sme.name: Signals intelligence subject matter expert
sme.length: 24 courses, about 8 years at two a term
sme.goal: Depth in statistical signal processing, with enough radio frequency and systems work that no part of a collection chain is opaque to you.
sme.tradeoff: Light on hardware. You will understand the receiver as a system but will not have built one. Take the collector track if you want the soldering iron too.

collector-full.name: Build your own collector
collector-full.length: 32 courses, about 11 years at two a term
collector-full.goal: Every stage of the signal chain, from the aperture to the exploited bits, with the bench work to build and troubleshoot each one. Organised as the signal travels.
collector-full.tradeoff: The longest path here by a wide margin. It buys the ability to design, build, operate and repair the whole device rather than one layer of it.
